 TeenWorks Employment Program
 More than just a job!
 Teens are employed by Montgomery County Recreation and placed in public sector and nonprofit jobs throughout the County.
 TeenWorks employees are provided mentorship and support by career professionals as they navigate through their first job. They engage in job readiness training with ongoing skill-building workshops and experiences, all while getting paid! They are placed in meaningful roles, which allow them to develop critical, marketable skills. TeenWorks opens the door to learning opportunities and facilitates connection to valuable community resources.

 Program Details
 Requirements  Interested students must:
 Be a Montgomery County resident and high school student
 Have availability to work a full year in the program
 Attend a mandatory TeenWorks employment information session to learn about the program, requirements for employment with Montgomery County Government and next steps, including an interview with the TeenWorks team
 Have the consent of a parent/guardian to be employed in this program
 Complete the employment application when the posting is available.

 Overview of TeenWorks Program
 TeenWorks benefits from an experiential learning model as career professionals and mentors utilize a hands-on approach in coaching teens to become empowered and prepared for the workforce. Through this workforce development program, they will work with professionals and have a variety of opportunities to choose from.
 Program Outline
 Program orientation with a specialist
 Orientation meeting with site placement
 Full-year commitment
 Attend 30 hours of workforce development training
 Work a maximum number of hours based on grade when first hired:  9th grade - 350 hours
 10th grade - 300 hours
 11th grade - 200 hours
 12th grade - 200 hours Schedule varies per site
 Weekdays, evenings and weekends
 Completion of three coaching sessions
 Develop and implement a capstone project
 Earn a certificate of completion and a letter of reference

 Frequently Asked Questions  
  What is a TeenWorks Host Site? 
 A TeenWorks Host Site is a partnership with a team or department within Montgomery County Government or a community organization, and the TeenWorks team (within Youth Development). TeenWorks are high school students who are seasonal/temporary employees for Montgomery County Recreation. They are placed at a Host Site where they can experience and learn a skilled trade through a combination of on-the-job training, coaching, and classroom instruction. The Host Site Supervisor and the TeenWorks team of Career Staff remain in contact to ensure the success of TeenWorks and the partnership.  
  How do I inquire about a partnership with TeenWorks to become a Host Site? 
 To initiate the conversation with the TeenWorks team, please complete the TeenWorks Host Site Interest Form. *We require Host Sites to provide structured work opportunities, on-site training and coaching, and supervision to Apprentices. 
  What are the benefits of hosting TeenWorks? 
 Hosting TeenWorks can provide several benefits, including access to motivated talent, the opportunity to train future employees according to your specific needs, introducing teens to career options, prepping for the workforce, and teaching teens transferable skills. 
  How long will TeenWorks remain at one placement? The duration of placement will vary depending on the scope of work and services agreed upon by both Montgomery County Recreation and the Host Site. TeenWorks assignments will range between 200 and 350 hours. 
  Are TeenWorks paid? 
 Yes, TeenWorks are temporary/seasonal employees of Montgomery County Recreation and are paid minimum wage. The TeenWorks Career Staff may request verification of hours worked to ensure accuracy. 
  What responsibilities do Host Sites have toward TeenWorks? 
 Host Sites are responsible for providing quality training and supervision, mentorship, and practical experiences to TeenWorks, ensuring they have the opportunity to learn and develop the skills necessary for the position. Promoting a safe and supportive learning environment is recommended. Additional details are included in the required Letter of Agreement, completed before program start. 
 What support and resources should you expect from Montgomery County Recreation’s TeenWorks Leadership as a Host Site partner? 
 Frequent meetings with the host to discuss TeenWorks involvement and the progress of their work to strengthen the effectiveness of the provided workforce development opportunity. Conducting an orientation session outlining program expectations and actively involving youth in the workplace. Collaborating with hosts to develop a distinctive career-based learning experience for their students and providing guidance on working effectively with high school youth. Each host will have access to a TeenWorks Coach/Career Staff to offer support to all parties. Facilitating additional career development workshops for TeenWorks to aid hosts and teens. Direct access to TeenWorks Career Staff and Coaches via email or phone. 
  How are TeenWorks matched with Host Site partners? 
 TeenWorks are matched with host partners based on their collected responses after completing an interest assessment. The TeenWorks program factors their interests, skills and career goals, as well as the specific requirements and opportunities offered by each partner organization. 
  How can the Host Site provide feedback or raise concerns about TeenWorks or the program? 
 Hosts can provide feedback or raise concerns about the program through regular communication with our TeenWorks Program team and participation in program evaluation activities.
